title: NEB Class 11 Physics — DC Circuits — 2024
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: State Kirchhoff's laws. A battery of 5 V total emf with 2 Ω total internal resistance drives a 5 Ω external resistor. Find the current.
questions.solution:
**KCL (junction rule):** the algebraic sum of currents at a junction is zero — charge is conserved.

**KVL (loop rule):** the algebraic sum of emfs round any closed loop equals the sum of the IR drops — energy is conserved.

Single loop: E = I(R + r) → I = 5/(5 + 2) = **0.71 A**.
questions.knowledgeNote: KCL ← charge conservation; KVL ← energy conservation — stating the conservation root earns the explanation mark.

questions.question: Resistors of 6 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in parallel across a 12 V battery. Find the current through each resistor and the total current.
questions.solution:
Parallel branches share the full voltage: I₁ = V/R₁ = 12/6 = **2 A**; I₂ = 12/3 = **4 A**.

Total I = 2 + 4 = **6 A** (check: R_eq = 2 Ω, 12/2 = 6 A ✓).
questions.knowledgeNote: In parallel, the smaller resistor hogs the current — current divides in the inverse resistance ratio.

questions.question: State the principle of the Wheatstone bridge and write its balance condition.
questions.solution:
Four resistors form a diamond; the bridge is **balanced** when no current flows through the middle galvanometer, so the two branch points are at equal potential.

Balance condition: **P/Q = R/S** (ratios of adjacent arms equal). An unknown resistance follows from three known ones.
questions.knowledgeNote: The metre bridge is a Wheatstone bridge stretched into a wire — same P/Q = R/S, with lengths standing in for two arms.

questions.question: A cell of emf 2 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω is connected to a 3.5 Ω resistor. Calculate the terminal voltage of the cell.
questions.solution:
Current I = E/(R + r) = 2/(3.5 + 0.5) = **0.5 A**.

Terminal voltage V = E − Ir = 2 − (0.5 × 0.5) = **1.75 V** (equivalently V = IR = 0.5 × 3.5 = 1.75 V).
questions.knowledgeNote: V = E only on open circuit — the moment current flows, Ir is lost inside the cell.

questions.question: Define drift velocity and derive the relation I = neAv_d.
questions.solution:
**Drift velocity** is the slow average velocity electrons acquire along a wire under an electric field (≈ mm/s).

In time t, electrons in length v_d·t cross a section: N = n·A·v_d·t carriers, charge Q = Ne = neAv_d·t. So I = Q/t = **neAv_d**.
questions.knowledgeNote: Signals travel near light speed (field propagation) while electrons merely drift — that is why the bulb lights 'instantly'.

questions.question: State the principle of a potentiometer. How is it used to compare the emfs of two cells?
questions.solution:
**Principle:** for a uniform wire carrying steady current, the potential drop per unit length is constant — balancing length ∝ emf.

Each cell in turn is balanced against the wire (null deflection): E₁/E₂ = **l₁/l₂**. Because readings are taken at null, the cell supplies no current — the true emf, not the terminal voltage, is compared.
questions.knowledgeNote: Null-method advantage: no current drawn from the test cell, so internal resistance never corrupts the result.
